units.function: A 6,316-line Tool Gateway orchestration service covering ephemeral and named bearer sessions, protocol rate limits, Profile-filtered discovery, policy decisions, approval pause/resume, signed arguments, Secret resolution, remote HTTP/local stdio/plugin execution, runtime slots, events and audit projections.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on Paperclip database tables, policy/access/Secret/runtime services, issue interactions, plugins, provider-specific configuration and Paperclip self-tools; routes and Agent/plugin callers depend on it. It is a broad Paperclip application/runtime service, not a neutral Connector port.
units.keyDataModels: GatewaySession, McpGateway/Token, Profile/Binding, Invocation, ActionRequest, Approval, IssueThreadInteraction, ToolCallEvent, AccessAuditEvent, Connection/CatalogEntry, Secret version snapshot and RuntimeSlot.
units.lifecycle: Authenticates a run/session or named token, discovers policy-visible Tools, records a decision and Invocation, parks risky work in approval/interactions, signs canonical arguments and remote target/Secret snapshots, atomically claims approved work, dispatches to builtin/plugin/remote/local runtimes, validates results and writes operational/audit projections.
units.testAssessment: Two first-party suites totaling 4,977 lines are broad, integration-heavy and use embedded PostgreSQL, Express/Supertest, real HTTP/SSE and local-process fixtures. They cover tenant/run binding, hashed tokens, distributed rate limits, policy denial, signed approval replay, target/Secret drift, SSRF, header redaction, runtime lifecycle and structured failures. Locally Vitest discovered both suites but skipped all 66 tests because embedded PostgreSQL support was unavailable, so no execution pass is claimed. Important omissions or codified conflicts include direct expired approval, policy/authority revocation after approval, human approver qualifications, crash/outbox recovery, provider idempotency, revoke races, plugin cancellation/timeout, audit retention, chunked oversize bodies and same-company self-tool least privilege.
units.designRationale: Provide one governed MCP/Tool execution plane for Paperclip Agents and external clients, with layered bearer authentication, Profiles/policies, human interaction cards, immutable reviewed arguments, Secret-version freshness and operational runtime supervision.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equivalent execution safety but must bind every side effect to an accountable human, ResponsibilityContract, exact permission/data contract and durable evidence lifecycle across vendor-neutral Connectors and cloud/local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE hashed opaque tokens, active run/tenant binding, database-atomic rate counters and execution claims, signed canonical arguments, live endpoint/catalog/Secret-version snapshot comparison, manual redirect/SSRF defenses, minimal subprocess environment, structured reason codes, redacted summaries and runtime health/recovery patterns. Reimplement as separate Session Authority, Policy/Approval, Connector Dispatch, Runtime Supervisor and Evidence/Outbox contexts behind Company OS ports.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service permits Agent decision identities in approval flows, lacks versioned accountable-human/ResponsibilityContract/data-egress binding, does not re-evaluate authority after approval, mixes decision resolver with executor, marks a request executed before the side effect completes, records quarantined post-side-effect output as denied/failed and persists action/interactions/events/audits nontransactionally. Static/local config can hold credentials outside the Secret boundary, replay keys omit key governance/run dimensions and several timeouts cannot prove cancellation.

units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL service integration tests for approval creation, direct approval/rejection, signed arguments, races, issue closure, elicitation, plugin result guards and Secret redaction.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises the Tool Gateway service and persisted database projections directly; it is downstream verification and contains Paperclip-specific approval and issue-interaction semantics.
units.keyDataModels: Invocation, ActionRequest, Approval, IssueApproval, IssueThreadInteraction, ToolCallEvent, audit/activity records, remote connection/catalog and heartbeat run.
units.lifecycle: Builds company/Agent/run fixtures, triggers Tool policy decisions and approvals, mutates decision projections, resumes execution and asserts terminal database/evidence state and redaction.
units.testAssessment: Strong on reviewed-argument integrity, same-run scoping, concurrent single execution, closed-issue blocking, fail-closed signatures, destructive formal approval, elicitation projection and malicious-result redaction. It omits expired direct approval, qualified-human authorization, post-approval revocation, rejection evidence completeness, provider idempotency, crash recovery, plugin timeout/cancellation and data-egress contracts. Current local run discovered but skipped the database suite; no pass is claimed.
units.designRationale: Keep a complex cross-table approval and Tool execution workflow behaviorally coherent with real database state rather than isolated mocks.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs executable tests for responsibility and effect semantics under concurrency and failure, including the distinction between authorization, dispatch, provider commitment, evidence quarantine and retry safety.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the embedded-database fixtures, signed-argument tamper tests, cross-run scope tests, Secret absence assertions and concurrent claim test. Replace Paperclip-specific issue cards with Company OS ResponsibilityContract/ApprovalDecision/Evidence assertions and add fault injection at every external-effect persistence boundary.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests allow Agent ids as approval decision makers, do not require an accountable human, and treat a malicious result returned after plugin execution as a failed/denied call rather than an executed effect with quarantined output.

units.function: Full Tool Gateway acceptance suite spanning HTTP routes, MCP protocol, named/ephemeral tokens, Profiles, remote/local/plugin transports, Secrets, approval, audit queries and runtime supervision.
units.dependencyDirection: Runs across routes, services, database, SDK demo server, local HTTP servers and runtime supervision; it is a system test suite coupled to Paperclip schema and UI-facing projections.
units.keyDataModels: Company membership/permission, Agent/run/issue/project, gateway/session/token/rate counter, application/connection/catalog, Profile/policy, Secret/binding/version/access, Invocation/ActionRequest/Event/Audit and RuntimeSlot.
units.lifecycle: Creates isolated tenants and execution fixtures, drives discovery/call/approval/revocation/audit/runtime flows over service and HTTP boundaries, injects protocol failures and verifies persisted scope, status and redaction.
units.testAssessment: Mature breadth includes cross-instance limit state, company isolation, SSE interoperability, Secret/header precedence, target/credential freshness, session/run invalidation, granular runtime permissions, capacity/backoff/stuck recovery and hosted-local fail-closed behavior. Missing stress/failure semantics include session revoke race, external-effect crash windows, no-length response bounds, cleanup retention, Profile replacement revocation, same-company self-tool authorization, plugin timeout and versioned human/data authority. Local execution skipped all database tests.
units.designRationale: Validate the production-shaped MCP execution plane end to end, including operational concerns often missed by feature-only suites.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equivalent compatibility and operational tests across managed-cloud and self-hosted execution while preserving independent domain semantics and a complete responsibility chain.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the real HTTP/SSE fixtures, multi-instance counters, SSRF/header/Secret matrices, deployment-profile tests and runtime recovery cases. Rebuild fixtures around Company OS principals, responsibility/data contracts, Connector capability attestations, effect receipts, transactional outbox and explicit cancellation/idempotency proofs.
units.responsibilityConflict: The suite proves Paperclip's run/issue/Agent attribution but repeatedly accepts Agent approval identities and never requires the human/contract/data authority that Company OS treats as core. Copying it unchanged would freeze the wrong governance model.
